name: sysml-editor
description: Graphical and model-aware editor for SysML v2

commands.title: Copy Document Annotations Library to Workspace

sysml.exclude.description: Glob patterns (relative to the workspace folder) of .sysml files that are not indexed. Applied together with files.exclude and search.exclude.

sysml.diagram.imageTheme.description: Theme of images saved or copied from a diagram: a fixed light theme, or the editor's current theme.

sysml.tree.followCursor.description: Reveal and select the tree node for the declaration under the text cursor.

enumDescriptions: Language Model Tools for in-editor agents, plus an MCP server for external agents (not registered with VS Code, so no duplicate tools).
MCP server only, also registered with VS Code. No Language Model Tools.
Language Model Tools only. No MCP server.
sysml.agent.channels.description: How AI agents reach the SysML tools. Changes apply without reloading.

sysml.agent.tutor.markdownDescription: Let an AI agent teach you the editor: it can point at things in diagrams and the requirements editor with a spotlight and a callout, and watch what you do (`sysml_ui_highlight`, `sysml_ui_wait_for_user`, `sysml_ui_state`, `sysml_ui_screenshot`). It cannot act for you. User-level only. Never available in an untrusted workspace. Every call is logged to the `SysML Agent UI` output channel.

sysml.agent.uiControl.markdownDescription: Let AI agents drive and observe the editor window through the `sysml_ui_*` tools (run allowlisted commands, answer prompts, act in diagrams). User-level only: a workspace cannot turn it on. Never available in an untrusted workspace. Every action is logged to the `SysML Agent UI` output channel.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_list_files
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the SysML v2 (.sysml) files of the workspace with their root package names and whether each has syntax errors. Standard library files are not listed. Use it first to find out what models exist; then use sysml_get_element_tree or sysml_get_element. Returns JSON: { files: [{ path, rootPackages, hasSyntaxErrors }] } with paths relative to the workspace root.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_get_element_tree
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Browse the ownership hierarchy of the SysML v2 model. Without `root` it starts at all root packages of the workspace; with `root` (a qualified name such as VehicleModel::Vehicle) it returns that subtree, which can also be a standard library element. `depth` is the number of levels returned (root level counts as 1; default 2, max 10). A node cut off by the depth limit has `truncated: true` and `childCount`; request that node's qualifiedName as `root` to go deeper. At most 500 nodes are returned; if that cap is hit the result says so, then request a subtree. Imports, comments and documentation are not shown. Elements without a name have a `locator` (owner, kind, ends) instead of a qualifiedName. Returns JSON: { nodes: [{ qualifiedName, kind, name, type?, children? }] }.

root.description: Qualified name of the element to start from. Default: all workspace root packages.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_get_element
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the details of one SysML v2 element by qualified name (for example VehicleModel::Vehicle): kind, name, short name, types, specializes/subsets/redefines, multiplicity, direction (in, out, inout), documentation, visibility, owner, owned members (name, kind, direction, type), relationship statements it owns (connect, bind, satisfy, ... with their ends), the file (workspace-relative) and 1-based line range of its declaration, and whether it is read-only standard library content. Use sysml_get_element_tree first to discover qualified names. A package declared in several files returns one entry per declaration. Returns JSON: { elements: [...] }. If nothing matches, an error names the closest existing prefix.

qualifiedName.description: Qualified name, segments separated by ::, quotes kept for names like 'My Part'.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_validate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check SysML v2 files for problems and return them as a list; an empty list means clean. Call it after writing or editing a .sysml file. Reports (1) syntax errors and (2) unresolved names, limited to what can be judged reliably: the type after ':' of a usage, supertypes (:>) of definitions, and import targets. It does NOT check redefinitions, subsetting, feature chains, expressions, or semantic rules. A file with syntax errors is not checked for unresolved names. `file` is a workspace-relative path; without it the whole workspace is checked. Reflects unsaved editor content. Returns JSON: { problems: [{ file, line, column, severity, message }] } with 1-based line and column. If `detailsPending` lists files, their syntax errors are still being computed: the problem shown for them is provisional ("details pending"); call again shortly for the precise errors.

file.description: Workspace-relative path of one file. Default: whole workspace.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_list_diagrams
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the diagram files (.sysmld) of the workspace. A diagram is a view of the SysML model (general, interconnection, requirements, action flow, state transition or sequence view) that stores which elements are shown and where, never the model itself. Returns JSON: { diagrams: [{ path, kind, root, nodeCount, parses, open }] } with paths relative to the workspace root; `parses: false` marks a file that is not a valid diagram (it then has `problems` instead of kind, root and nodeCount). `open` is true when the diagram is open in an editor, in which case its in-memory content is listed. Use sysml_read_diagram to see one diagram's content.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_read_diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read one diagram: its kind, root element, and every node and edge with the element it shows (name, qualified name, kind, types, relationship ends), containment (`parent`), stored positions (x, y, w, h, relative to the parent node, when known), edge routes and unresolved references (items whose element no longer exists). If the diagram is open in an editor, its in-memory content is described, including unsaved changes. Returns JSON { path, open, unsaved, kind, root, sources, nodes, edges, unresolved }. With `includeImage: true` the result also carries a PNG of the diagram (light theme, at most 1600 px wide) rendered by the diagram view as a second content item; with `format: "svg"` it carries the SVG text instead, in the JSON as `image.svg`. If the diagram is not open, it is rendered in a short-lived editor tab beside the current one that is closed again at once (focus and the active editor stay as they are); if rendering fails or times out, the JSON is returned with an `image` note saying the image is unavailable and why. Large diagrams are truncated with a note.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the .sysmld file, as listed by sysml_list_diagrams.

includeImage.description: Also return an image of the diagram. Default false.

format.description: Image format with includeImage: png (default, a second content item) or svg (the SVG text in the JSON).

languageModelTools.name: sysml_create_diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a new diagram file for a model element and return its path and description. `root` is the qualified name of the element shown as the diagram's root (for example Vehicle::Car); the diagram is pre-populated with the root and its direct members (for a requirements view, the requirements and what the relationships tie them to). `kind` is general (definitions and usages with specialization, composition and typing; use cases with their actors and includes), interconnection (parts nested in a part, with ports and connections), requirements, actionFlow (root: an action or action def; its actions, start/done, fork/join/decide/merge nodes, successions with guards and flows), stateTransition (root: a state or state def; its states, entry/do/exit actions and transitions with trigger, guard and effect) or sequence (root: an occurrence, part or interaction that owns `message` usages; lifelines and the messages between them in time order). A root that does not fit the kind is refused with the reason. `elements` optionally restricts the members shown to those qualified names. `path` is workspace-relative and must end in .sysmld; by default the file is created beside the root's source file under the element's name, and an existing file is never overwritten (a numbered name is used, or an explicit existing path is rejected). The new diagram has no stored positions; the editor lays it out when it is opened. Changes the diagram file only, never the model. Not available in an untrusted workspace.

root.description: Qualified name of the root element, e.g. Vehicle::Car.

kind.description: general, interconnection, requirements, actionFlow, stateTransition or sequence.

elements.description: Qualified names of the members to show (at most 200). Default: all visible direct members.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the new .sysmld file. Default: beside the root's source file.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_add_to_diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Add model elements to an existing diagram as nodes (relationship statements such as satisfy or connect become edges when both ends are on the diagram). `elements` are qualified names. Elements already on the diagram are left alone. Changes the diagram only, never the model, as one edit: if the diagram is open in an editor the change is applied to the open document as an undoable, unsaved edit (the tab shows it as modified); if it is not open the file is written. Returns JSON with `applied` (editor, file or none), what was added and the diagram as it is now. Not available in an untrusted workspace.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the .sysmld file, as listed by sysml_list_diagrams.

elements.description: Qualified names of the elements to add (at most 200).

languageModelTools.name: sysml_remove_from_diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Remove nodes or edges from a diagram by their ids (from sysml_read_diagram). Removing a node also removes its child nodes and every edge attached to any of them. Only the diagram changes: the model and the .sysml files are never touched. One edit: applied as an undoable, unsaved edit when the diagram is open in an editor, written to the file otherwise. Returns JSON with `applied` (editor, file or none), `removed` and the diagram as it is now. Not available in an untrusted workspace.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the .sysmld file, as listed by sysml_list_diagrams.

ids.description: Node or edge ids to remove (at most 200).

languageModelTools.name: sysml_layout_diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Arrange all nodes and edges of a diagram again (automatic layout), discarding manual positions. If the diagram is open in an editor this runs the editor's Auto-layout command: the new layout is shown at once as an undoable, unsaved edit. If it is not open, the stored positions and routes are cleared in the file so that the layout is computed the next time the diagram is opened or rendered (the returned description then has no positions). Only the diagram changes. Returns JSON with `applied` (editor, file or none) and the diagram as it is now. Not available in an untrusted workspace.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the .sysmld file, as listed by sysml_list_diagrams.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_apply_diagram_aspect
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Apply a saved aspect of a diagram (a named subset of its nodes: only those nodes and the lines among them are drawn), or clear the applied aspect so every node is drawn again. `action` is apply (with `name`) or clear. Aspects are listed by sysml_read_diagram in the diagram's style and are saved by the user in the editor. A layout edit: only the diagram changes, never the model; applied as an undoable, unsaved edit when the diagram is open in an editor, written to the file otherwise. Returns JSON with `applied`, `edit: "layout"`, the aspects and the diagram as it is now. Not available in an untrusted workspace.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the .sysmld file, as listed by sysml_list_diagrams.

action.description: apply a named aspect, or clear the applied one.

name.description: apply: the name of the aspect.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_show_hide_diagram_members
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show or hide the direct parts and ports of one node of a general, interconnection or requirements diagram. `node` is a node id from sysml_read_diagram; `show` and `hide` are the names of its parts and ports (own or inherited). Showing adds the member as a node (a port on the border) with the lines between drawn elements; hiding removes only that node and its lines from the diagram. A layout edit: the model is never changed, and inherited members are listed but never edited. Applied as an undoable, unsaved edit when the diagram is open in an editor, written to the file otherwise. Returns JSON with `applied`, `edit: "layout"`, `added`, `removed`, the `members` available (name, kind, drawn) and the diagram. Not available in an untrusted workspace.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the .sysmld file, as listed by sysml_list_diagrams.

node.description: Id of the node, from sysml_read_diagram.

show.description: Names of parts and ports to draw.

hide.description: Names of parts and ports to remove from the diagram.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_get_editor_context
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read what the user is looking at in the diagram editor right now: the active diagram, the node or line under the pointer, the selected elements and the other open diagrams. `focused` says whether that diagram is in the active tab; when the user is elsewhere (for example in the chat) it is the diagram they last used that is still visible. Use it to resolve "this", "here" or "the selected part" in the user's request. Returns JSON { activeDiagram: { path, kind, root, focused } | null, hovered: item | null, selected: item[], openDiagrams: string[] }. `activeDiagram` is null when no diagram is visible (then `hovered` is null and `selected` is empty). Each item is { id, type: node | edge, element?, resolved } as in sysml_read_diagram (a line the view derives from the model, such as typing or composition, has `derived: true` with its relationship and end node ids instead of an element): `id` is the diagram node or edge id; `element` has the qualified name (or, for an unnamed statement such as a succession, a locator) to use with the other tools. `hovered` is cleared when the pointer leaves the diagram or the diagram is hidden. `openDiagrams` lists the other diagrams open in editors. Read-only.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_create_element
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a new element in the model by inserting its declaration into the owner's .sysml source, exactly as the diagram palette and the tree's Add Child do (minimal text edit, indentation copied, a body created when the owner ends in `;`). `owner` is the qualified name of the package, definition or usage to add it to (a feature a usage only inherits cannot be the owner; add to the usage itself). `kind` is one of: package, part def, port def, attribute def, item def, action def, state def, requirement def, verification def, part, port, attribute, item, action, state, requirement, verification, fork, join, decide, merge. `state` and `state def` add states (inside a state or state definition they are nested states); `fork`, `join`, `decide` and `merge` add control nodes and are only allowed inside an action or action definition: give them a name, because successions refer to nodes by name. Optional `type` (qualified name or name of a definition of the matching kind; an import is added when needed), `multiplicity` (e.g. 0..1 or *), `shortName` and `documentation`. With `diagram`, a node for the new element is also placed on that diagram. The edit is applied directly, the file is saved, and the user can undo it in one step. Returns JSON with the new element's qualifiedName, the files changed and (with `diagram`) the placement. Refused for files with syntax errors, in an untrusted workspace and for names that already exist in the owner. Not for deleting (sysml_delete_element) or changing (sysml_set_element_properties).

owner.description: Qualified name of the element to add to, e.g. VehicleModel::Vehicle.

name.description: Name of the new element (quoted automatically when it needs quotes).

type.description: Type of a usage: qualified name or name of a definition, e.g. Engine or Powertrain::Engine.

multiplicity.description: Multiplicity of a usage, e.g. 4, 0..1 or *.

documentation.description: Documentation text, written as a doc comment.

diagram.description: Optional workspace-relative path of a .sysmld diagram to place the new element on (as a node, or an edge for a relationship). The diagram file is updated on top of its last saved state; pending layout in an open diagram stays unsaved.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_delete_element
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Delete an element from the MODEL: its whole declaration (with its body, owned members and attached documentation) is removed from the .sysml source and saved, and nodes for it are removed from every diagram file. This is different from sysml_remove_from_diagram, which only removes a node from a diagram and leaves the model untouched. References to the deleted element elsewhere are not rewritten and will no longer resolve (check with sysml_validate); the result reports how many remain (`remainingReferences`) and where. `element` is the qualified name; an unnamed succession, transition or message (they have no qualified name) is given as `statement`, the `locator` that sysml_read_diagram lists for it ({ owner, kind, ends, index? }). Deleting an action, state, control node or message also deletes the successions, transitions and flows that connect it, in the same edit (listed in `alsoDeleted`). A succession written as `then x;` inside a node declaration cannot be deleted on its own. A feature that a usage only inherits from its definition (for example Model::vehicle1::engine, declared in Vehicle) cannot be deleted from the usage: the error names the declaring definition. Applied directly; the user can undo it in one step. Refused for files with syntax errors and in an untrusted workspace.

element.description: Qualified name of the element to delete.

statement.description: An unnamed succession, transition or message: its locator.

fingerprint.description: The `fingerprint` that sysml_read_diagram lists with the locator; the call is refused when the statement is no longer the one that was read.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_rename_element
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Rename an element: its declaration and every reference to it that resolves in the workspace (qualified references change only the matching segment; names are quoted when needed), and every diagram file that refers to it. `element` is the qualified name, `newName` the new name. Returns JSON with the new qualifiedName, `referencesUpdated`, and `couldNotJudge` (mentions of the old name that the tool could not decide about, with a few locations: check them). Refused when the new name clashes with another member, for inherited features (rename them in their definition), for files with syntax errors and in an untrusted workspace. Applied directly; one undo step for the user.

element.description: Qualified name of the element to rename.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_set_element_properties
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change properties of an element in its .sysml source: `name`, `shortName`, `type` (of a usage: qualified name or name of a definition; an import is added when needed), `multiplicity` and `documentation`. Give only the properties to change; an empty string removes shortName, type, multiplicity or documentation. All changes are one edit. A feature that a usage only inherits cannot be changed from the usage (the error names the declaring definition). Refused for files with syntax errors and in an untrusted workspace. Returns JSON with the files changed and the qualifiedName after the edit.

type.description: Type of a usage; empty removes it.

multiplicity.description: Multiplicity, e.g. 4, 0..1 or *; empty removes it.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_create_relationship
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a relationship statement in the model. `kind: "connection"` adds `connect <source> to <target>;` to `owner` (the element that contains both ends, e.g. the part def or usage that owns the two parts); `source` and `target` are qualified names of the connected parts or ports, written as feature chains relative to the owner. `kind: "specialization"` writes `:> <target>` on the declaration of the definition `source` (`part def Frigate :> Ship`); `source` and `target` are qualified names of two definitions of the same kind; a different kind, itself, an existing specialization, a cycle and an inherited or library source are refused with the reason. `kind: "dependency"` adds `dependency from <source> to <target>;` to `owner` (default: the package that holds `source`); `source` is the client and `target` the supplier, both qualified names. `kind: "satisfy"` adds `satisfy <requirement> by <by>;` to `owner` (default: the package that holds `by`); `requirement` and `by` are qualified names. Names are written so they resolve from the owner; an import is added when needed. `kind: "verify"` adds `verify <requirement>;` to the objective of a verification case (SysML v2 allows verify only there): give `verificationCase` (qualified name of an existing verification case; its objective is created when missing) or `newVerificationCase` (a name; a new `verification` containing the objective is created in `owner`, default the package of the requirement). `kind: "derivation"` adds `#derivation connection { end #original ::> <original>; end #derive ::> <derived>; ... }` (derivation is not a keyword) to `owner` (default: the package of the first derived requirement) and `private import RequirementDerivation::*;` when missing; `original` and `derived` (a list) are qualified names of requirements. `kind: "succession"` adds `first <source> then <target>;` (with `guard`: `first <source> if <guard> then <target>;`) to `owner`, an action or action definition, after the two nodes; `source` and `target` are member names or qualified names of its actions or control nodes, or `start` and `done`; a succession that already exists is refused. `kind: "transition"` adds `transition first <source> [accept <trigger>] [if <guard>] [do <effect>] then <target>;` to `owner`, a state or state definition; `source` and `target` are its states (`trigger`, `guard` and `effect` are source text, parsed before anything is changed and refused with the syntax error when invalid). `kind: "message"` adds `message [name] [of <itemType>] from <from> to <to>;` to `owner`, an occurrence, part or interaction, written as `then message ...;` right after its last message so it comes last in time order; `from` and `to` are names of the parts taking part. With `diagram`, the new edge is also placed on that diagram when both ends are shown; a specialization is a derived edge, drawn automatically when both definitions are on the diagram (the result reports `placed: true, derivedEdge: true`). Applied directly, saved, one undo step. Refused for files with syntax errors and in an untrusted workspace. Returns JSON with the files changed.

kind.description: connection, specialization, dependency, satisfy, verify, derivation, succession, transition or message.

owner.description: Qualified name of the element that receives the statement. Required for a connection.

source.description: connection or dependency: qualified name of the first end; specialization: the specializing definition.

target.description: connection or dependency: qualified name of the second end; specialization: the definition specialized.

requirement.description: satisfy: qualified name of the requirement.

by.description: satisfy: qualified name of the satisfying element.

verificationCase.description: verify: qualified name of an existing verification case (def or usage).

newVerificationCase.description: verify: name of a new verification case to create.

original.description: derivation: qualified name of the original requirement.

derived.description: derivation: qualified names of the derived requirements.

guard.description: succession or transition: the guard as source text, e.g. level > 3.

trigger.description: transition: the trigger as source text, e.g. TurnOn (written after accept).

effect.description: transition: the effect as source text, e.g. action logEvent (written after do).

from.description: message: name of the sending part.

to.description: message: name of the receiving part.

name.description: message: optional name of the message.

itemType.description: message: optional item type (qualified name or name of a definition).

diagram.description: Optional workspace-relative path of a .sysmld diagram to place the new element on (as a node, or an edge for a relationship). The diagram file is updated on top of its last saved state; pending layout in an open diagram stays unsaved.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_set_transition
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change the trigger, guard and effect of an existing transition. The whole transition statement is written again from its parts as `transition [name] first <source> [accept <trigger>] [if <guard>] [do <effect>] then <target>;`, exactly as the State Transition View's properties panel does (a shorthand transition inside a state is rewritten in this explicit form). Identify the transition by `element` (qualified name, when it is named) or by `statement` (the locator sysml_read_diagram lists: { owner, kind: "transition", ends, index? }). Give only the parts to change; an empty string removes a part. The text is parsed before anything is applied; invalid text is refused with the syntax error and nothing changes. Applied directly, saved, one undo step. Refused in an untrusted workspace.

element.description: Qualified name of a named transition.

fingerprint.description: The `fingerprint` that sysml_read_diagram lists with the locator; the call is refused when the statement is no longer the one that was read.

trigger.description: Trigger text (after accept); empty removes it.

guard.description: Guard text (after if); empty removes it.

effect.description: Effect text (after do); empty removes it.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_read_requirements_document
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read a package as a specification document, the same projection the requirements editor's Document view shows, as Markdown: the title (from a @DocumentRoot annotation, else the package name), a table of contents, numbered sections (1, 1.1, ...; nested packages), their paragraphs (doc and comment text), requirement items (id, name, text, satisfied by / verified by / derived from) and appendices (packages annotated @Appendix, lettered A, B, ...). Section numbers are generated from the nesting and source order and are not stored in the model. Each heading and each requirement is followed by a marker such as `<!-- qn: VehicleSpec::Performance::accel -->` with the qualified name to pass to the edit tools (sysml_set_element_properties, sysml_create_requirement, sysml_create_relationship, ...). `package` is the qualified name of the root package (a nested package reads just that part). Output is limited to 60000 characters; the end then says it was truncated. Read-only.

package.description: Qualified name of the package, e.g. VehicleSpec.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_create_requirement
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a requirement in a package: `requirement <'ID'> name;` (or `requirement def` with `definition: true`), with optional documentation as a doc comment, exactly as the requirements editor's Add Requirement does. `owner` is the qualified name of the package (or definition) to add it to. Text containing the comment terminator star-slash is stored as star-backslash-slash. Applied directly, saved, one undo step. Refused for files with syntax errors, existing names and in an untrusted workspace. Returns JSON with the new element's qualifiedName and the files changed.

owner.description: Qualified name of the package to add the requirement to.

id.description: Requirement id, written as the short name <'id'>.

documentation.description: The requirement text, written as a doc comment.

definition.description: Create a requirement def instead of a requirement usage.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_read_verification_matrix
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read the requirements verification matrix of a package, the same rows, columns and status as the requirements editor's Matrix view: one row per requirement, nested and numbered by ownership (1, 1.1, ...; packages are section rows), with satisfied by, verification method, verified by and status. The method comes from the standard VerificationMethod metadata on the verification case (@VerificationMethod { kind = VerificationMethodKind::test; }): inspect, analyze, demo or test. Status is `not satisfied` (no satisfy statement, own or counted from a parent requirement), `partly satisfied` (a requirement definition, or a requirement it owns, whose usages are not all satisfied; `usages` gives satisfied and total), `no verification` (satisfied, no verification case verifies it, own or counted from a parent requirement) or `covered`. Satisfaction counted from elsewhere has `via` set. Pass/fail results are not part of the model and not shown. `package` is the qualified name of the package. `format` is `json` (default: summary and rows with qualified names, to pass to the edit tools), `markdown` or `csv` (the editor's export text). At most 1000 rows. Read-only.

package.description: Qualified name of the package, e.g. VehicleSpec.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_dodaf_generate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Generate a DoDAF 2.02 architecture description document from the model under `root` (a package or element, by qualified name). Views are selected from DoDAF metadata annotations (see the DoDAF library, SysML: Add DoDAF Library). Table views (AV-1, AV-2, CV-1, OV-4, OV-5a, SV-5a, StdV-1, DIV-2) are written as Markdown tables; diagram views (CV-2, OV-1, OV-2, OV-5b, OV-6c, SV-1, SV-2, SV-4, SV-10c) get a diagram beside the root's source file, named <Name>-<VIEW>.sysmld, created if missing and reused if present (an existing .sysmld is never rewritten), and an image rendered by the diagram view into <folder>/images/. OV-1 uses the picture named by @OV1Graphic { path } (workspace-relative) instead of a drawing when present. If the diagram view cannot draw, the tables are still written and the diagram sections say so. The document is <folder>/<RootName>.md (default folder docs/dodaf; a document this tool wrote, and its images, are replaced; any other existing file there is refused unless `overwrite: true`; diagrams are never overwritten). With `plan: true` nothing is created or written: the result lists what would be produced. Returns JSON: document path, per-view status (written, empty, skipped, planned) with diagram and image paths, `gaps` (model problems found in the tables) and `missing` (annotation definitions no element uses, per view): fix these and run again. Not available in an untrusted workspace.

root.description: Qualified name of the architecture root, e.g. Mission.

views.description: View ids to produce. Default: all 17.

format.description: Image format for diagram views. Default svg.

overwrite.description: Replace <folder>/<RootName>.md and images that were not written by this tool. Default false: such files make the call fail.

plan.description: Only report what would be produced and the gaps; write nothing.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_command
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Run an editor command as the user would from the command palette or a menu: any `sysml.*` command, or core undo, redo, save, save all, back and forward (ids: undo, redo, workbench.action.files.save, workbench.action.files.saveAll, workbench.action.navigateBack, workbench.action.navigateForward). Other ids are refused. `args` are the command's arguments (JSON values; strings that are file paths must lie inside the workspace). The call returns when the command finishes or as soon as it opens a prompt (a quick pick, input box, confirmation or dialog); the result lists the open prompts, which you answer with sysml_ui_answer. Delete commands ask for confirmation, which you must answer explicitly. Works only when the user has turned on the setting sysml.agent.uiControl in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

command.description: The command id, e.g. sysml.createDiagram or undo.

args.description: Arguments passed to the command, at most 8.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_answer
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Answer an open prompt (a quick pick, multi-pick, input box, confirmation, choice dialog or save dialog), as listed by sysml_ui_command or sysml_ui_state. Give exactly one of: `pick` (an item label), `picks` (item labels, for a multi-pick), `text` (for an input box; a validation message comes back and the box stays open), `confirm: true`, `path` (for a save dialog; must be inside the workspace), or `cancel: true`. `prompt` is the prompt id; omitted it is the oldest open prompt. A prompt left open times out as cancelled. Needs sysml.agent.uiControl on, in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

prompt.description: Id of the prompt; default the oldest open one.

pick.description: The label of the item to choose.

picks.description: Labels of the items to tick.

text.description: The text for an input box.

confirm.description: true confirms; to decline use cancel.

path.description: File path for a save dialog, inside the workspace.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_state
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Observe the editor window: whether UI control is enabled, the active editor and its dirty flag, the selection in open diagrams, open context menus and their items, the undo and redo labels of each diagram, the messages shown to the user (information, warning, error) since the last read (each is reported once), open prompts, navigation history, and what the clipboard holds (none, text, image or elements; never its content). When UI control is off or the workspace is untrusted it answers `enabled: false` with the reason instead of failing. Read-only; every call is logged.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Act in an open diagram as a user does, and observe what it shows once the gesture has settled (the diagram is opened when it is not open). `path` is the .sysmld file. `gesture` has a `kind` and its fields: select {id, shift?}, drag {id, dx, dy, steps?, hold?}, resize {id, handle, dx, dy}, key {key, shift?, ctrl?, meta?} (Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy and paste elements, Delete removes), rubber {x0, y0, x1, y1}, contextmenu {id} (opens the context menu; the result's `menu` lists its item labels), menuItem {label} (clicks an item of the open menu by label, e.g. "Align Left"), menu {id, action}, drop {names, x?, y?}, palette {item, id?, x?, y?, name?, hold?}, inline {text?, end?}, dblclick {id, area?}, descriptions {show}, legend {show} (toggles), connect {source, target, relation?}, connectDrag, reconnectDrag, selectEdge {id}, dragSegment, dragBend, dblclickEdge, labelDrag, labelResize, labelMenu, inlineRename {id, text, commit}, hover {id?}, hoverNode {id}, wheel {deltaY, ctrl?}, quickBar {item?}, and flush (no change, only observe). The result: the selected ids, the open menu's labels, node boxes (id, x, y, w, h), legend labels, the inline editor, and what the clipboard holds. Questions the gesture opens (a picker, a name box) are listed by sysml_ui_state and answered with sysml_ui_answer. Needs sysml.agent.uiControl on in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

path.description: The .sysmld diagram file, inside the workspace.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_requirements
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Act in the requirements editor of a package (`package`: qualified name) or a .sysml file (`file`), opening it when needed, and observe it. `action`: open {view?}, view {view: table|matrix|document}, click {selector}, input {selector, value, event?: change|input} (add a requirement inline, edit its text), key {selector, key, alt?}, dragToc {fromQn, ontoQn, position: before|after} (reorder or nest a section in the table of contents), mouse {type, selector, at?, dy?}, exportMatrix {format: csv|markdown, path} (written inside the workspace), observe. Selectors are the editor's data-testid or data-qn attributes, e.g. [data-testid=add-root-requirement], tr[data-qn="P::R1"], [data-testid=toc-entry][data-qn="P::Sec"]; expand and collapse are clicks on the section head. The result: the view, outline, requirement items, matrix rows, pending edits, and the notice shown. Needs sysml.agent.uiControl on in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

package.description: Qualified name of the package scope.

file.description: Path of a .sysml file scope, inside the workspace.

type.description: Mouse event type for action mouse.

path.description: Output file for exportMatrix, inside the workspace.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_tree
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use the SysML Model tree. `op`: list {parent?, depth? (1 to 4, default 1), limit?} lists the visible nodes with id, label, context value, depth and selection; select {nodes: [one id]} selects and reveals one node (ids from list; the tree API cannot select several, so more than one is refused); command {command, node?} runs a command the tree offers: the view title commands (sysml.tree.newFile, sysml.tree.newFolder, sysml.tree.refresh, sysml.tree.changeView, sysml.tree.clearSearch; no node) or a node's context commands (sysml.tree.rename, sysml.tree.delete, sysml.tree.deleteFile, sysml.tree.addChild, sysml.newDiagram, sysml.showInDiagram, sysml.openRequirementsEditor, sysml.goToDefinition, sysml.addToActiveDiagram, sysml.tree.newFile and newFolder on folders). A command not offered for that node is refused. The result lists the prompts the command opened, which sysml_ui_answer answers. collapseAll collapses the tree. Needs sysml.agent.uiControl on in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

parent.description: Node id to list below; default the roots.

nodes.description: The one node id to select.

node.description: The node a command acts on.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_screenshot
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A PNG of what a webview shows right now, as the user sees it, in the active theme: the selection, open context menu, legend, compartments, palette and properties panel of a diagram (`path`), or the requirements editor of a `package` or `file` (open it first with sysml_ui_requirements). Only that webview is captured, never the screen. Unlike sysml_read_diagram this is the live editor, not the export. Needs sysml.agent.uiControl on in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

path.description: A .sysmld diagram file, inside the workspace.

package.description: Qualified name of a requirements editor package scope.

file.description: A .sysml file of a requirements editor scope.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_highlight
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Point at something in the UI to teach the user: a spotlight and a callout (plain text, at most 280 characters) in a diagram (`path`, with `node` = a node id, or `selector` = a data-testid/data-qn CSS selector) or in a requirements editor (`package` or `file`, with `selector`), which is brought to the front first. For VS Code's own chrome use `chrome` (modelTree, treeNewFile, treeNewFolder, commandPalette with `command`): nothing can be drawn there, so the view is revealed (or the Command Palette opened) and the result describes where the target is, which you pass on to the user in words. The user dismisses a highlight with Esc or the callout's close button; it never changes the model. A new highlight replaces the last. Works with sysml.agent.tutor or sysml.agent.uiControl on, in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

text.description: The callout, plain text; cut to 280 characters.

node.description: A node id in the diagram.

package.description: Qualified name of a requirements package.

file.description: A .sysml file for the requirements editor.

selector.description: A CSS selector in the webview, e.g. [data-testid=add-root-requirement].

command.description: For chrome commandPalette: the command id to show.

languageModelTools.name: sysml_ui_wait_for_user
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Wait until the user does something in the editor (a gesture in a diagram or requirements editor, a sysml.* command, a selection or editor change), then report what it was as {event: {kind, id?}} (kinds and ids only, never text). Your own actions are not reported. Returns {event: null, timedOut: true} after `timeoutSeconds` (default 60, at most 300). Use it after highlight to see the user try the step. Works with sysml.agent.tutor or sysml.agent.uiControl on, in a trusted workspace; every call is logged.

walkthroughs.title: SysML: First Steps
walkthroughs.description: Find your way around the model tree, create a file and open the requirements editor.

steps.title: Browse the model tree
steps.description: Open the **SysML Model** view in the Activity Bar to see files, packages and elements.

steps.title: Create a file
steps.description: Select [New File]($(command:sysml.tree.newFile)) and name it with a `.sysml` extension.

steps.title: Open the requirements editor
steps.description: Right-click a package and choose Open Requirements Editor.

walkthroughs.title: SysML: Diagram Basics
walkthroughs.description: Create a diagram, place and connect elements, and save it.

steps.title: Create a diagram
steps.description: Right-click a package and choose New Diagram.

steps.title: Place an element
steps.description: Pick an item from the palette and click the canvas.

steps.title: Connect elements
steps.description: Drag from a node's handle onto another node.

steps.title: Save the diagram
steps.description: Press Ctrl+S to keep the layout.
